title: Excel Basics: Grid & Values
description: Master cell grid coordinates, entering values, and formatting currency and numbers.

steps.title: Understanding the Spreadsheet Grid
steps.content: Excel is composed of vertical columns labeled with letters (A, B, C...) and horizontal rows labeled with numbers (1, 2, 3...). The intersection of a column and row is called a Cell (e.g., A1).

steps.title: Interactive Challenge: Enter Data into Cell A1
steps.content: Click on cell A1 in the Excel grid below and type the number 250 into the cell or formula bar.
steps.hint: Click cell A1 at the top-left of the grid and type 250.

quiz.question: What is the cell reference at the intersection of column C and row 5?
quiz.explanation: Excel cell references always list the column letter first, followed by the row number (e.g., C5).

title: Mastering Excel Formulas (=SUM)
description: Write basic formulas starting with '=' and calculate sums and averages with =SUM() and =AVERAGE().
objectives: Understand why all Excel formulas start with = equal sign

steps.title: The Power of Formulas
steps.content: Every formula in Excel must begin with an equal sign (=). The =SUM() function adds together all numbers in a specified range of cells.

steps.title: Interactive Challenge: Calculate Total with =SUM()
steps.content: In cell A4 of the Excel simulator, type '=SUM(A1:A3)' and press Enter to compute the total sum!
steps.hint: Select cell A4, type =SUM(A1:A3) and press Enter.

quiz.question: Which symbol MUST be typed first when writing a formula in Excel?
quiz.explanation: All Excel formulas must start with an equal sign (=) so Excel knows to evaluate an expression rather than treat it as plain text.

quiz.question: Which formula correctly calculates the sum of cells A1 through A5?
quiz.explanation: =SUM(A1:A5) is the correct standard Excel function for summing a range.
